messages.subject: smallcase: 8% of your negative reviews are about support, not product
messages.body:
Hi {first_name},

I pulled smallcase's recent public Play Store reviews and sorted the substantive ones by what the complaint is actually about. Of 66 negative reviews with real text in them, 8% are about the support channel itself rather than the product - no response, tickets left open, repeat follow-ups.

Two of them, verbatim: "Customer service can be improved. CC is acting only as postman, raised issue 45..."
and "Faced a transaction error in mutual fund and raise query for the same which..."

The reason I find that split interesting rather than just bad: complaints about the channel behave differently from complaints about the product. They tend to be the ones where the customer already knew what they wanted and could not get an answer, which is the cheapest category to fix and the most expensive to leave alone.

Does that match what you see in your own contact mix, or do your store reviews skew differently from your ticket queue?

{sender}

messages.subject: Re: smallcase — the metric that hides this
messages.body:
Following up with the part I think is actually useful, whether or not we ever speak.

I built an eval harness over 18 real support queries from Indian wealth and fixed-income operations, and scored three agent configurations on whether they DISPOSED of each query correctly, rather than on how many they deflected:

Naive retrieval:      67% automated, 39% correctly disposed, 8 confidently wrong
Routed + integrated:  72% automated, 94% correctly disposed, 0 confidently wrong

Near-identical deflection rates. The difference is entirely in whether the system answers from the customer's own record or from a help article.

If your current support tooling reports deflection rate but not disposition correctness, that gap doesn't appear anywhere in your reporting.

{sender}

{first_name} — sent you a note on support complaint mix at smallcase. No reply needed if it isn't a live problem.

One thing I'd value your read on regardless: when a customer writes in saying the outcome contradicts what they expected - money not received, a form submitted but not applied - does that reach a human at smallcase, or does a bot take it? I have yet to find a platform where the honest answer is the second one.

messages.subject: Closing the loop — smallcase
messages.body:
Last one from me.

I'll leave the query taxonomy and the eval harness with you either way. They're useful independently of us, and you can run them against whatever you have in production today.

If support contact mix becomes a priority later in the year, I'm easy to find.

{sender}
